Attribution/IP rejection, signup, UTC login days, guarded grants, artwork, email, handler-specific SQL errors and configured Slack effects have source-paired/local regressions. Slack keeps source payloads and empty-token serialization but deliberately bounds each effect to ten seconds, three attempts and a two-second Retry-After cap. Referral identity uses the TCP peer or explicitly trusted backend proxy X-Real-IP, and canonical historical inet aliases share a quota; these are intentional source differences. Referrer/IP quotas and milestone counts are serialized in SQL; reward image, inbox/email delivery and pending-state completion share a local transaction after the provider response is persisted. Actual source partial-failure receipts and local concurrent PostgreSQL cases are compared; simultaneous decision ordering is strengthened beyond source. A reward-tier grant retains reward_tier until its downstream notification and image complete. A committed pre-POST claim prevents concurrent or restarted workers from reissuing the non-idempotent provider request; a confirmed response is persisted before downstream work. With social writes enabled, a fleet-leased drain selects at most 64 due rewards per pass every 60 seconds, and failed attempts defer eligibility by one minute. The reward_paid receipt retains the tier, provider result and confirmed notification marker; an image retry skips a notification already recorded as delivered. Missing campaign configuration remains retryable before claiming. A claimed request without a confirmed response, including migrated historical pending rewards without a paid receipt, requires provider reconciliation and is not automatically retried; confirmed responses resume downstream delivery without another login. Local reward completion rolls back together on SQL failure. Exactly-once external reward issuance is not claimed. This recovery differs from the source, which commits the grant and does not retry a failed reward. Referral deny checks read the shared in-process explorer snapshot instead of fetching the list on each write. Every serving process refreshes the merged database mirror/local overlay every 30 seconds with a five-second pass timeout, even when mirrors or fleet jobs are disabled; failed refreshes retain the last snapshot. Reloads are serialized within each process. This is eventual propagation, not immediate revocation or identical source freshness. The receipt migration imports existing paid tiers and responses while preserving their notification completion marker. Migration 0024 is not safe alongside pre-0024 binaries even on schema v3: stop all old binaries, login consumers and writers before migrating, then resume only compatible code. Object-valued historical paid responses remain confirmed even with incomplete image metadata; repair that metadata without another provider POST. Native login recording commits independently of provider work; quarantined rewards remain pending for reconciliation without reissuing a POST.
